title: Treasury, IRS Announce Process for Tax Guidance Following DOJ Final Order on Medical Marijuana Rescheduling
summary: The Treasury and IRS announced plans to issue guidance clarifying federal tax consequences for medical marijuana businesses following DOJ's rescheduling of certain marijuana products from Schedule I to Schedule III under the Controlled Substances Act. The guidance will address how Section 280E (which disallows deductions for Schedule I/II substance trafficking) applies to affected businesses, including expense apportionment and a transition rule for the first full taxable year including the rescheduling effective date.
key_points: DOJ Final Order places FDA-approved marijuana products and state-licensed medical marijuana in Schedule III; unlicensed marijuana remains Schedule I
Section 280E currently disallows deductions and credits for businesses trafficking in Schedule I or II controlled substances
Rescheduling removes Section 280E as a barrier for affected businesses to claim deductions and credits
Forthcoming guidance expected to clarify expense apportionment for businesses with multiple activities
Transition rule will apply rescheduling for the full taxable year that includes the Final Order's effective date
Guidance will benefit medical marijuana businesses by enabling them to claim standard business deductions
